name: Bahrain

facts.religion: Muslim about 70% (Shia majority among citizens), large Christian and Hindu expatriate communities

system_note: A constitutional monarchy in name; power sits with the Al Khalifa family.
snapshot: Hit hard by Iranian missiles aimed at the US Fifth Fleet, Bahrain's Sunni monarchy answered sympathy for Iran among its Shia majority with mass arrests.
culture: Bahrain was the ancient Dilmun civilisation, a trading hub between Mesopotamia and the Indus, and its pearling heritage is UNESCO-listed. The Formula One Grand Prix has run in Sakhir since 2004. Ashura processions are central to Shia life, and the island's mix of Arab, Persian and South Asian communities shows in its food and markets.
society: Bahrain diversified early into banking and aluminium as its oil ran low, and it depends on Saudi Arabia, linked by a causeway, for support. Foreign workers make up about half the population. The 2011 uprising was crushed with Saudi help, and opposition societies have been dissolved. Bahrain normalised relations with Israel in 2020.

story: Bahrain is a small island ruled by a Sunni royal family over a population that is majority Shia, the same branch of Islam as Iran's. In 2011, when Shia-led protesters filled Manama's Pearl Roundabout calling for reform, Saudi troops crossed the causeway to help crush them. Bahrain also hosts the US Navy's Fifth Fleet. So when the US and Israel went to war with Iran in 2026, the old fault line cracked open.

Bahrain was among the Gulf states hit hardest by Iranian drones and missiles aimed at US forces. Some Shia Bahrainis mourned Ayatollah Khamenei, killed in the opening strikes, or posted sympathy for Iran; a few cheered hits on US bases. The state responded with mass arrests. By late March, rights groups counted more than 200 detained, mostly Shia, many for social media posts or mourning, including some pro-government Shia figures (AFP via Al-Monitor). On 9 May, the interior ministry announced the arrest of 41 people it said belonged to a group tied to Iran's Revolutionary Guard, and overnight raids picked up dozens of leading Shia clerics (AP via ADN, The New Arab). Dozens have been stripped of citizenship. Analysts warn the crackdown could reignite the sectarianism Iran has exploited before, at the moment Bahrain most needs its people united.
briefing.power: A constitutional monarchy in name, with power concentrated in the Al Khalifa family. The king appoints the prime minister, currently Crown Prince Salman, and the 40-member upper house; the elected 40-seat lower house has limited power. The main Shia opposition party, Al-Wefaq, has been banned since 2016.
briefing.holders: King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa, with Crown Prince and Prime Minister Salman bin Hamad.
